name: Matteo Ricci's road to Beijing
summary: An Italian Jesuit learns Chinese, dresses first as a Buddhist monk and then as a Confucian scholar, and works his way north for eighteen years until the Wanli emperor lets him stay in Beijing. His world map shows China the continents; his journals, published after his death, show Europe Ming China from within.

stops.note: He sails for the Indies in March.
Four years teaching and studying in Portuguese India.
The first Jesuit house inside China. A first world map is printed here.
Expelled from Zhaoqing, he moves north and puts on the robes of a scholar.
He writes On Friendship in Chinese.
He meets Xu Guangqi, who will become his closest Chinese collaborator.
He presents clocks to the Wanli emperor and is allowed to live in the capital until his death in 1610.
